title: A small-slope graph lying in a slab around T0 is nearly parallel to T0
statement:
Let q, q0 be linear isometries of R^{n+l}, T0 := rotatedPlane q0 = q0(R^n x {0}), v : R^n -> R^l, y in R^{n+l}, s > 0, and eps, h real. Assume:
- |v x1 - v x2| <= eps |x1 - x2| for all x1, x2 in the closed ball B_s(0) of R^n;
- infDist(y + q(graphPoint x (v x)), T0) <= h for every x in B_s(0).
Then infDist(q(graphPoint e 0), T0) <= (h/s + eps) |e| for every e in R^n.
lean_statement: ∀ {n ℓ : ℕ} (q q₀ : Amb n ℓ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] Amb n ℓ) (v : Rn n → Rn ℓ) (y : Amb n ℓ) (s ε h : ℝ), 0 < s → (∀ x₁ ∈ closedBall (0 : Rn n) s, ∀ x₂ ∈ closedBall (0 : Rn n) s, ‖v x₁ - v x₂‖ ≤ ε * ‖x₁ - x₂‖) → (∀ x ∈ closedBall (0 : Rn n) s, infDist (y + q (graphPoint x (v x))) (rotatedPlane q₀ : Set (Amb n ℓ)) ≤ h) → ∀ e : Rn n, infDist (q (graphPoint e 0)) (rotatedPlane q₀ : Set (Amb n ℓ)) ≤ (h / s + ε) * ‖e‖
